title: `FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown`/`mulDivUp` round-trip asymmetry enables share inflation in ERC4626-style accounting
impact: When integrators use `mulDivDown` for deposit→shares and `mulDivUp` for shares→assets inconsistently (or vice versa), an attacker can round-trip tiny amounts to extract value. Specifically, `mulWadDown(mulWadUp(x))` style round trips can lose/gain 1 wei per operation; in a vault, repeated 1-wei extractions across many operations or a manipulated first-depositor donation (share inflation attack) compounded with downward rounding on `convertToShares` lets an attacker mint shares cheaply and withdraw more than deposited.
